projects.title: Automated image analysis of tau fibrils in the human Alzheimer's disease brain
projects.summary: The project aims to detect tau fibrils within tau tangles in human Alzheimer's disease brain tissue, imaged with correlative light and electron microscopy, and measure their twist to study tangle stages. The student would develop a Python image analysis workflow for denoising, line detection, segmentation and machine learning-based pixel classification.

projects.title: Analysis of dendritic spine changes using deep-learning encoding in a latent space
projects.summary: The project aims to develop a deep-learning system that reconstructs the temporal evolution of dendritic spine shapes. Spine shapes from time-lapse 3D microscopy would be encoded into a low-dimensional latent space to classify single-spine behaviours and study neural plasticity.

projects.title: From PDE to Cell Imaging: A Multiresolution Framework for Fourier Ptychography
projects.summary: Build a PDE/wavelets-inspired multiresolution reconstruction algorithm for Fourier ptychographic microscopy, representing the high-resolution complex image with box-spline basis functions and refining from low to high frequencies to avoid poor local minima in the non-convex loss. The student will combine an existing Python Fourier ptychography library with a box-spline modelling library.

projects.title: Multigrid Solver For Non-Uniform Sampling With TV Regularization
projects.summary: Develop a fast solver for the non-uniform interpolation problem based on the multigrid scheme. The underlying image is represented with box-splines, with a focus on TV-based regularizers, implemented in PyTorch.

projects.title: Penalized Maximum Likelihood Approach for Deconvolution of Microscopy with Learned Convex Regularizer
projects.summary: The project addresses deconvolution of microscopy images, where measurements are a convolution of the ground truth with a known blur kernel and are corrupted by Poisson noise. The student will derive a variational formulation of the problem, solve it with a suitable optimization approach, and benchmark a state-of-the-art learned convex data-driven regularizer.

projects.title: Prediction and survival analysis of ovarian cancer through multimodal fusion of radiomic and multiomic data.
projects.summary: A six-month master's project on personalized treatment of high-grade serous ovarian cancer. It aims to fuse radiomics features from CT/MRI with multiomics data to build predictive and survival models, with attention to feature robustness and reproducibility. The work is part of the ERC-funded MROMICS initiative and is based at the Montpellier Cancer Institute (PINKCC lab).

projects.title: Sparse Unrolled Auto-Encoders for Interpretable Analysis of Neural Data
projects.summary: The project investigates sparse autoencoder-style interpretable deep learning for understanding neural computation. It builds on the DUNL (Deconvolutional Unrolled Learning) framework, which unrolls ISTA for convolutional sparse coding, and explores unrolling the greedy Matching Pursuit algorithm as a simpler-to-tune and easier-to-explain alternative.

projects.title: Diffusion Models for Magnetic Resonance Imaging Reconstruction
projects.summary: Develop and evaluate diffusion-model priors for reconstructing MRI images from undersampled k-space data. The work compares baseline 2D diffusion reconstructions with the lab's in-house deep learning method, explores new architectures and reconstruction frameworks, and assesses the feasibility of 3D diffusion reconstruction for MRI.

projects.title: Inverse Problems with ℓ1 Regularization: Extreme Points of the Regularization Polytope and Analysis vs Synthesis Formulations
projects.summary: Determine the extreme points of the regularization polytope {x : ||Lx||₁ ≤ 1} defined by a regularization operator L, in order to analyze solution structure and enable a synthesis formulation of ℓ1-regularized inverse problems. The student studies background on inverse problems and sparsity, then designs and implements an algorithm to compute these extreme points for a given L.

projects.title: Discretization of Non-Uniform Sampling Problems with Exponential Splines
projects.summary: Recover a continuous-time signal from noisy non-uniform samples by solving an inverse problem with generalized total-variation (gTV) regularization. The student studies L-spline theory and exponential splines, discretizes the problem with B-splines, and solves the resulting finite-dimensional optimisation problem with suitable algorithms.

projects.title: Likelihoods for Hawkes Processes
projects.summary: The student will study a recently proposed binned likelihood for estimating the excitation kernel of Hawkes processes, which is easier to optimise than the classical likelihood when many events are observed or the process is near or above criticality. Tasks include simulating Hawkes process trajectories, implementing estimators based on the classical and binned likelihoods, and comparing their strengths and weaknesses.

projects.title: Sampling from Learned Regularizers
projects.summary: The project studies posterior sampling for linear inverse problems using energy-based models built from learnable potential functions applied to linear filter responses. The goal is to implement and analyze sampling algorithms such as the (annealed) Metropolis adjusted Langevin algorithm for uncertainty quantification.

projects.title: Improving Optimization Algorithms for Ptychography Phase Retrieval
projects.summary: Explore and improve the convergence and efficiency of optimization algorithms for ptychography phase retrieval. The student will implement and compare strategies such as quasi-Newton and conjugate gradient, with explicit or automatic-differentiation gradients, and possibly investigate GPU acceleration schedules and adaptive hyperparameter selection.

projects.title: High-Dimensional Gaussian Sampling: Cholesky versus Markov
projects.summary: Compares three approaches to generating high-dimensional Gaussian samples: exact Cholesky-factorization linear algebra, iterative Markov Chain Monte Carlo, and Perturb-and-Map. The goal is to find the best trade-off between computational speed and statistical accuracy for large-scale inverse problems.

projects.title: Vector-Valued Inverse Problems: B-Spline Discretization and Identification of Matrix Differential Operators for Regularization
projects.summary: Design and implement a Python package for two-dimensional vector spline functions based on matrices of differential operators (MDOs), and validate it on a synthetic or real-world problem. The project also studies vector-valued inverse problems regularized with an MDO, aiming to identify or learn a suitable MDO from observations of correlated vector-valued signals.

projects.title: Exploring Global Youth Art Through AI: A Semantic Analysis of the IMAJ Collection
projects.summary: Semantic analysis of a database of more than 100,000 drawings by young artists aged 3 to 25 from 150 countries, collected by IMAJ. The project will evaluate large language models on curated subsets before scaling up to generate textual interpretations and enrich the metadata of the collection.

projects.title: Investigating steerable wavelets to build Parseval frames
projects.summary: Develop a learned, convex regularizer for image reconstruction based on a parametric, steerable wavelet framework that controls filter scale and orientation with a compact parameter set. The regularizer is trained via denoising and validated on diverse inverse problems using accelerated gradient methods.

projects.title: Training Complex-Valued Denoisers for Phase Retrieval
projects.summary: The project aims to train a denoiser that operates directly on complex-valued data, regularizing magnitude and phase jointly for phase retrieval. The student will study amplitude-phase coupling across imaging modalities, build complex-valued datasets, and compare Plug-and-Play, diffusion and flow-matching paradigms against magnitude/phase splitting.

projects.title: Continuous-Domain Phase Retrieval in Dimension One
projects.summary: Develop and benchmark a coarse-to-fine (multiscale) numerical solver for recovering a complex-valued continuous-domain signal from magnitude-only linear measurements. The solver starts with Wirtinger Flow at a coarse scale and propagates estimates up the resolution hierarchy, and is compared with single-scale Wirtinger Flow with spectral initialization at full resolution.

projects.title: 789 – Spine motion replication
projects.summary: Replicate the spine motion of quadruped locomotion with fewer actuators than a fully articulated spine would need, reducing weight and mechanical complexity. The project is 100% software.

projects.title: 784 – Modeling zebrafish sensorimotor integration using simulation and robots
projects.summary: Model zebrafish sensorimotor integration using neuromechanical simulation and the ZBot fish-like robot, in an ongoing collaboration with Duke University. Possible avenues include improving the FARMS simulation framework, applying deep reinforcement learning to sensory-motor circuits, and studying visually-guided behaviors.

projects.title: 734 – Firmware development for ENVIROBOT
projects.summary: Continue the development of ENVIROBOT by adapting the existing firmware to a new electronic board and extending it with new functionality. The work is mainly software on an embedded microcontroller platform.

projects.title: 783 – Paleorobotics of Armored Tail Strikes: Simulation, Compliance, and Energy Dissipation in Extinct Mammalian Weapons
projects.summary: Use paleorobotics to test whether extinct armored mammals could generate powerful tail-club strikes, by building MuJoCo and SIMM/OpenSim-type models of a tendon-driven tail and mapping strike energy dissipation. Optional work includes a biomimetic carapace and a tendon-driven tail prototype, split between EPFL and University of Zurich.

projects.title: 782 – Radio communication module on 169.4 MHz
projects.summary: Finalize a prototype bidirectional serial link based on a CC1120 radio chip at 169.4 MHz, by redesigning the PCBs, improving communication software and stability, adding a simple user interface on the microcontroller, and adding flow control on the robot side.

projects.title: 729 – Robotic paleontology: tail strike defense
projects.summary: Design, build and control a life-sized robotic tail to replicate a dinosaur's club-tail strike, and measure impact force and velocity using fossil-based bone-like material at Empa Dübendorf. The thesis combines mechanical design, microcontroller programming, force measurements and data analysis.

projects.title: 786 – (New!) User-Centric Multimodal Interaction for Assistive Robotic Environments
projects.summary: Study the everyday challenges of wheelchair users and investigate how multiple user interfaces (markerless body-language tracking, LLM/VLM natural-language control, tablet) can give accessible control of mobile robotic furniture. The student can further develop or evaluate one interaction modality.

projects.title: 785 – (New!) Mobile Manipulation of Assistive Robotic Furniture
projects.summary: Integrate a robot arm with a mobile robotic furniture platform and develop a whole-body controller so that a mobile table can fetch objects for a wheelchair user, e.g. bringing a cup of water. The goal is an end-to-end demonstration in MuJoCo simulation and in the real world.

projects.title: Project 1: Comparing Representational Hierarchies in Neural Networks
projects.summary: Investigates how layer selection and aggregation shape conclusions about representational similarity between neural networks. The goal is a principled way to compare models across their full representational hierarchies, distinguishing isolated layer matches from agreement across the hierarchy, and reassessing evidence for representational convergence.

projects.title: Project 2: What Do Language Models Need from 3D Encoders?
projects.summary: Studies what 3D encoders (point clouds or Gaussian splats) contribute when connected to a language model for 3D scene reasoning, and how 3D representations could be learned to be more useful to LLMs. Starts from existing 3D encoders and a controlled 3D LLM pipeline, and extends to modeling spatial organization of cells.

projects.title: Project 3: Learning patient-level predictions from the spatial proteome
projects.summary: Develops a multiple instance learning approach for patient-level prediction from spatial single-cell proteomics data, aggregating information across spatial scales from single cells to niches and whole-tissue organization. Evaluation on public multiplexed imaging cohorts with patient-level outcomes such as cancer survival, including data efficiency and agreement of attended regions with known pathology.

projects.title: Project 4: Improving agents for single-cell genomics and biomedical discovery
projects.summary: Aims to improve the reasoning capabilities of LLM-based agents for single-cell biology tasks using agentic reinforcement learning, so that the agents can plan, execute computational workflows, and formulate hypotheses for biomedical discovery.

projects.title: Accelerating Safe ML Systems
projects.summary: Explores how to use RDMA (Remote Direct Memory Access) communication to make distributed machine learning training both fast and secure, for example secure collaborative or robust ML training.

projects.title: Distributed Resource Efficient Inference Engine
projects.summary: Projects on the distributed inference engine Anyd, which aggregates heterogeneous hardware over any network into a unified cluster that schedules GenAI inference and handles failures transparently. The goal is to address the challenges of its distributed, automatically managed nature.

projects.title: Extracting Block I/O Stream Representations from Filesystems
projects.summary: Investigate how filesystems (e.g., ext4, XFS, F2FS, Btrfs) transform application file operations into block I/O seen by SSDs, and derive a minimal set of block I/O streams that captures the steady-state device-level behavior relevant to SSD performance and write amplification.

projects.title: SSD-Aware RL for Data Placement in Storage Systems
projects.summary: Study whether exposing SSD-internal state (garbage collection activity, write amplification, utilization, wear) to a reinforcement-learning data-placement agent, and optimizing jointly for performance, write amplification, wear balance and energy, yields better policies for heterogeneous SSD arrays than existing black-box approaches.

projects.title: Profiling Automated Verifiers
projects.summary: Build a profiler that attributes SMT-based verifier solving time (e.g., Dafny, KLEE with Z3/CVC5) across the verifier stack, distinguishes useful from useless work and brute-force search from precise reasoning, and evaluates whether it helps pinpoint real-world performance root causes.

projects.summary: Studies whether coverage reported by Cortex-M firmware rehosting systems reflects meaningful exploration, or is affected by artifacts of the emulated environment such as MMIO, interrupts, timers and DMA. The project will build a framework to record coverage with execution context and develop techniques to improve coverage-guided fuzzing of rehosted firmware.

projects.title: Ownership-Aware Bug Hunting in Rust Crates
projects.summary: Aims to build an ownership-aware bug detection mechanism for Rust crates that models ownership transitions induced by unsafe APIs, such as bitwise copies that lead to double-free bugs. The goal is to detect ownership-related bugs the compiler cannot enforce.

projects.summary: Detect events in signals by signal processing to characterize an optical fiber. The page gives only the title and project level.

projects.summary: Learn molecular anisotropic diffusion using self-supervised deep learning. The page gives only the title and project level.

projects.title: Python software development for automated single-cell protein isolation with a CryoWriter
projects.summary: Develop Python software to automate single-cell protein isolation with a CryoWriter. The page gives only the title and project type.

projects.title: Collecting a large dataset on human similarity and preference perception
projects.summary: The project aims to collect a large crowdsourced dataset of similarity and preference judgements (e.g. 'Is A more similar to B or C?', 'Which of A, B, C do you prefer?') across several object types such as food, books, movies and faces. The student will extend an existing web app to add datasets and query types, then build a machine learning pipeline to evaluate the data and support the experiment.

projects.title: Generating random graphs with a given treewidth of k
projects.summary: The goal is to investigate and develop approaches for generating random graphs with a given prior (e.g., independent edges as in Erdős–Rényi graphs) that have treewidth k, since no implementation currently exists for this task.

projects.title: Analyzing Network Cascades to Infer Graph Properties
projects.summary: The project asks what can be inferred about an unknown network from multiple observed cascades spreading over it. It aims to test whether the super-spreader detection method of Mossel and Sridhar can be extended to noisy cascade observations, and whether properties such as communities, clustering coefficients, or degree assortativity can be inferred from a limited number of cascades.

projects.title: Stochastic proximal first-order algorithm
projects.summary: Find a batch-free stochastic proximal first-order algorithm achieving O(1/epsilon) gradient oracle complexity for an epsilon-global optimum when the objective is smooth and satisfies 2-PL (or quadratic growth).

projects.title: Computational methods for Chance Constraint Optimization
projects.summary: The project aims to study and compare several existing computational methods for optimizing over chance-constrained sets, namely sample average approximation, scenario approximation, p-efficient points, and penalised convex difference, in practice.

projects.title: SIS Model Simulator with Dynamic Vaccination and Visualization
projects.summary: Develop a high-performance, modular simulator in Python or Julia for the SIS (Susceptible-Infected-Susceptible) disease model on networks, supporting node and edge vaccination strategies, adjustable infection and recovery probabilities, and dynamic interventions. The project also aims to build interactive real-time visualization tools to observe and analyze vaccination effects and SIS dynamics.

projects.title: Distinguishing Random Graphs via Distance Measures
projects.summary: The project develops a method to distinguish graphs (trees, Erdős–Rényi graphs with a chosen density, and complete graphs) from First Passage Percolation distance measurements taken from a source vertex. It includes simulating FPP on various graphs, evaluating the density thresholds at which ER graphs are distinguishable, and theoretically bounding the method's accuracy.

projects.title: Estimation the Number of Clusters in Mixture Models using Data Thinning
projects.summary: The project investigates using data thinning, a way to split each data point into independent training and test parts, to infer the number of clusters k in a mixture model. For exponential-family mixtures with known k, it builds on k-means adapted to Bregman divergences.

projects.title: Exploring good transformations of edge weights for spectral clustering
projects.summary: The project aims to identify optimal edge weight transformations (e.g. logarithmic scaling or thresholding) for spectral clustering algorithms on weighted networks, to maximise community separation in the embedded space. It also explores whether such transformations can be identified in a data-driven manner, building on spectral embedding as a Gaussian mixture model and recent clustering results for mixture models.

projects.title: Matrix Factorisation With Comparison Data
projects.summary: Study the performance of gradient descent on a nonconvex matrix factorization problem for learning from pairwise comparison data. Students generate synthetic data from a generative model and analyse how gradient descent behaves as a function of noise, sparsity and other data properties.

projects.title: Bayesian Optimization for Soft Clustering
projects.summary: The project aims to design and implement clustering algorithms that use Bayesian Optimization to tune hyperparameters, such as the degree of freedom of Student's t-distribution mixture models, and to compare them with state-of-the-art clustering methods.

projects.title: Web scrapping for hierarchical clustering
projects.summary: Collect text and metadata from Wikipedia and/or arXiv and evaluate how well a newly proposed rigorous definition of hierarchy agrees with the hierarchy derived from the metadata.

projects.title: Robust Collaborative Filtering
projects.summary: Design a robust collaborative filtering technique that provably bounds the influence of each user on others, so that a minority of (possibly fake) accounts cannot manipulate the content recommended to the rest. The student will review the literature, modify existing algorithms, and run experiments.

projects.title: SAT‑Driven Exact and Heuristic Treewidth & Decomposition
projects.summary: Investigate SAT-based methods for exact treewidth computation and tree decomposition, and for heuristic approximate tree decompositions. The student would implement SAT/MaxSAT encodings of tw(G) ≤ k, reconstruct explicit decompositions, design relaxed encodings for polynomial-time heuristics, and benchmark against state-of-the-art solvers on the PACE 2017 Treewidth competition.

projects.title: Robustness and Performance of Spectral Clustering Methods for Community Detection
projects.summary: The project aims to systematically evaluate spectral clustering techniques for community detection, using normalized, unnormalized Laplacians and adjacency matrices, through numerical experiments on synthetic and real-world networks. It also seeks to identify conditions where methods differ and explore metrics such as Chernoff information to guide method selection.

projects.title: Recommender System with hierarchical structure
projects.summary: Explore hierarchical structures in the user-item matrix to refine the low-rank assumption of matrix factorization recommender systems, and test whether this improves performance. Also develop a recommender that is robust to malicious users.

projects.title: When does effective-resistance sparsification preserve infection dynamics?
projects.summary: Investigates whether effective-resistance sparsification of mobility networks preserves SIR infection dynamics, depending on the degree distribution of the original graph. The goal is to study the observed trichotomy (no for short-tailed, yes for a specific heavy-tailed regime, no for very heavy tails), formulate a conjecture, and sketch a proof.

projects.title: ER Graph Discovery via Independent Distance Measurements
projects.summary: Develop a method to distinguish Erdős–Rényi graphs of different edge densities from weighted shortest-path distance measurements between random vertex pairs, with simulations, accuracy and sample-complexity evaluation, and theoretical accuracy bounds. Builds on existing asymptotic results for complete graphs and Erdős–Rényi first-passage percolation.

projects.title: Causal Subgoal Discovery for Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
projects.summary: Implement and study the Strict Subgoal Execution (SSE) hierarchical RL framework, reproduce its core method, and add causal intervention techniques to improve it. The project also involves learning a structural causal model over key state factors to propose causal subgoals for a manager/worker hierarchical policy, benchmarked on a latent-variable benchmark against HRL baselines.

projects.title: Accelerating ecological connectivity analysis with graph neural networks
projects.summary: Proposes using graph neural networks to learn coarser graph embeddings of fine-scale landscape features, so that resistance distance-based gene flow predictions become computationally tractable at higher spatial resolution. Directions include graph coarsening strategies, approximation error bounds, and validation on synthetic and real ecological data.

projects.title: High-performance differentiable AMG in JAX with GPU acceleration
projects.summary: Develop an algebraic multigrid (AMG) solver in JAX that supports automatic differentiation and GPU acceleration, for scientific machine learning workflows requiring differentiable iterative linear solves. The work involves analysing existing Python and Julia AMG implementations and designing a JAX-compatible architecture.

projects.title: Evaluating Multiview Structure Preservation in Dimensionality Reduction
projects.summary: Evaluate several widely used dimensionality reduction methods on benchmark multiview datasets to assess how well they preserve multiple latent views of the data. If time permits, propose a new dimensionality-reduction method that explicitly preserves multiview structure.

projects.title: Finding Slow Components in a Graph
projects.summary: The project studies how many random shortest-path distance queries are needed to identify a set of vertices V_1 whose incident edge weights are much larger than the rest of a weighted graph with exponentially distributed weights. It includes simulations on a range of graphs, evaluation of accuracy and sample complexity, and theoretical accuracy bounds.

projects.title: Reusable Foundations for Probabilistic Proofs in Lean
projects.summary: Develop a reusable Lean library on top of Mathlib providing foundations for probability (beyond existing martingales, concentration inequalities and CLT, e.g. Markov chains, random walks, couplings), so probabilists can formalize their results more easily. If time allows, the library would be used to formalize a paper on random graphs and branching processes.

projects.title: Formalizing probabilistic tools (Markov chains, couplings) in Lean
projects.summary: Bring existing and new tools for probability (martingales, CLT, Markov chains, couplings) together into a coherent Lean framework that makes formalization easier for probabilists.

projects.title: Recovering slow components of an information spreading process on a graph
projects.summary: Study a simple information spreading process on a graph where some parts transmit information more slowly. The project asks how to recover the slow component from transmission-speed measurements, comparing random and adaptive measurement strategies.

projects.title: High-performance algebraic multigrid solver in JAX
projects.summary: Develop an algebraic multigrid (AMG) linear solver in JAX with automatic differentiation and GPU acceleration, for gradient-based optimization in scientific machine learning and differentiable physics.

projects.title: Graph neural networks for fast ecological connectivity analysis
projects.summary: Use a graph neural network to map fine-scale landscape features onto lower-dimensional graph representations, accelerating resistance-distance computations for gene flow prediction and conservation planning.

projects.title: Dimensionality reduction preserving multiple latent views
projects.summary: Evaluate whether popular dimensionality reduction methods preserve multiple independent latent structures (multiview information) in high-dimensional datasets, and possibly develop a new method that preserves several views at once.

projects.title: Causality-aware hierarchical reinforcement learning with Strict Subgoal Execution
projects.summary: Learn a structural causal model over latent state factors from exploratory rollouts, identify causal bottlenecks (keys, switches, doors) as subgoals, and train a policy to reach them with Strict Subgoal Execution for long-horizon, sparse-reward tasks.

projects.title: SAT/MaxSAT methods for tree decompositions
projects.summary: Use SAT and MaxSAT solvers to compute exact and approximate tree decompositions of graphs, evaluated on the PACE 2017 Treewidth benchmarks.

projects.title: Generating random graphs with a given treewidth
projects.summary: Design and implement methods that generate random graphs with a prescribed treewidth k, in Python or Julia.

projects.title: Large online study on human similarity and preference choices
projects.summary: Help conduct a large online study collecting human similarity and preference choices, forming the dataset for research on probabilistic choice models and recommender systems. Requires strong web development and data science skills.

projects.title: Inferring structure of random graphs from sampled shortest-path distances
projects.summary: Infer structural properties of random graphs from sampled weighted shortest-path distances, distinguishing Erdős–Rényi graphs of different densities and detecting planted high-degree nodes or cliques, with analysis of accuracy and sample complexity.

projects.title: Effective-resistance sparsification and infection dynamics
projects.summary: Investigate when effective-resistance sparsification preserves the infection dynamics of the original graph, across short-tailed and heavy-tailed degree distributions.

projects.title: Hierarchical structures in matrix factorization for recommender systems
projects.summary: Explore hierarchical structures within the user-item matrix to improve low-rank matrix factorization, and develop a recommender that is more resilient to malicious users.

projects.title: Robustness of spectral clustering under different Laplacian operators
projects.summary: Study the robustness and performance of spectral clustering methods across different Laplacian operators, to clarify when and why performance differs and give guidelines for choosing a method.

projects.title: Recommendation algorithm limiting per-user influence
projects.summary: Develop a personalized recommendation algorithm that limits the influence each user can have on the others, to resist manipulation.

projects.title: Evaluating a definition of hierarchy against Wikipedia/arXiv metadata
projects.summary: Collect text and metadata from Wikipedia and/or arXiv and measure how well a recently proposed rigorous definition of hierarchy agrees with the hierarchy derived from the metadata.

projects.title: Clustering algorithms using Bayesian optimization
projects.summary: Participate in the design, implementation and evaluation of clustering algorithms that exploit Bayesian optimization.

projects.title: Simulations of gradient descent on nonconvex matrix factorization
projects.summary: Run simulations to test the performance of gradient descent on a class of nonconvex problems arising from matrix factorisation.

projects.title: Optimal edge weight transformations for spectral clustering
projects.summary: Identify edge weight transformations for several spectral clustering algorithms that maximize community separation in the embedded space.

projects.title: Choosing the number of clusters K with held-out validation
projects.summary: Address the choice of the number of clusters K, where selecting K by fitting and validating on the same data can overfit and bias results, and study alternative validation schemes.

projects.title: Distinguishing tree, Erdős–Rényi and complete graphs via First Passage Percolation
projects.summary: Simulate First Passage Percolation on random graphs and use shortest-path distances from a source node to distinguish tree, Erdős–Rényi and complete graphs, identifying structural thresholds and accuracy bounds.

projects.title: SIS epidemic simulator with vaccination strategies and interactive visualization
projects.summary: Develop an SIS model simulator in Python or Julia with advanced vaccination strategies and dynamic infection and recovery rates, plus interactive tools to monitor disease dynamics in real time.

projects.title: Numerical experiments for chance-constrained optimization
projects.summary: Carry out numerical experiments comparing several known methods for solving chance constraint optimization problems.

projects.title: Batch-free stochastic proximal first-order algorithm
projects.summary: Find a batch-free stochastic proximal first-order algorithm with O(1/epsilon) gradient oracle complexity for smooth objectives satisfying 2-PL (or quadratic growth).

projects.title: Inferring graph structure from infection times of cascades
projects.summary: Given infection times of vertices from one or several cascades (such as epidemic waves) spreading through an unknown graph, infer what can be learned about the graph's structure.

projects.title: Comparing community detection algorithms and their communities
projects.summary: Group several community detection algorithms and investigate the properties of the communities that each one finds.

projects.title: Theoretical analysis of a dynamic Bayesian optimization algorithm
projects.summary: Contribute to the theoretical understanding of a dynamic Bayesian optimization algorithm.

projects.title: Choosing the optimal number of clusters K (second formulation)
projects.summary: Determine the optimal number of clusters K for n data points when K is unknown, avoiding the bias that arises when the same data is used for fitting and validating clustering models across different K values.

projects.title: Class for handling mixed graphs
projects.summary: Design and implement a class for handling mixed graphs, in Python or Julia.

projects.title: Combining user feedback in the form of ratings and comparisons
projects.summary: Study how to best collect and combine feedback from different users, given as ratings and pairwise comparisons.

projects.title: Simulating an infectious process on graphs against state-of-the-art simulators
projects.summary: Simulate a mathematical model of an infectious process on a graph and compare the simulator to state-of-the-art simulators on real-world data.

projects.title: Data staleness criterion in dynamic Bayesian optimization
projects.summary: Implement and study the performance of a criterion measuring data staleness in a dynamic Bayesian optimization context.

projects.title: Effect of degree heterogeneity on community detection
projects.summary: Study whether the heterogeneity of node degrees in real graphs (few hubs and many low-degree nodes) helps or degrades community detection algorithms.

projects.title: Applications of graph sparsification
projects.summary: Study different applications of graph sparsification.

projects.title: Porting the Flatland railway simulator to Julia
projects.summary: Speed up the Python-based Flatland challenge simulator, in which trains must reach destinations quickly without colliding, by translating it to Julia. Julia knowledge is not required.

projects.title: Efficient graph algorithms for the Julia ecosystem
projects.summary: Contribute to the Julia graph ecosystem by implementing efficient graph algorithms. Prior Julia or graph theory knowledge is not required.

projects.title: Algorithmic stability and generalization of stochastic first-order methods
projects.summary: Use notions of algorithmic stability to study the generalization of stochastic first-order optimization, including variance reduction and adaptation, and whether SGD performs implicit regularized empirical risk minimization.

projects.title: Multi-armed bandit recommendation from user choices
projects.summary: Design and implement recommendation algorithms that learn user preferences from choices among sets of items, focusing on multi-armed bandit algorithms.

projects.title: Second-order methods in Atari games
projects.summary: Apply second-order methods in complex environments such as Atari games and compare them empirically with first-order methods in sample complexity and robustness to initialization.

projects.title: Clustering networks with time-varying interactions
projects.summary: Propose and study methods for clustering networks in which interactions between nodes vary over time.

projects.title: Effect of community structure on source identification of spreading processes
projects.summary: Observe how the community structure of a network affects the identification of the source of a spreading process such as disease spreading.

projects.title: Comparing generalization error of SCRN and momentum-based SGD in RL
projects.summary: Empirically compare the generalization error of two stochastic optimization algorithms used in reinforcement learning, SCRN and momentum-based SGD.

projects.title: Global properties of the expected return in reinforcement learning
projects.summary: Check global properties of the objective function (the expected return) in various reinforcement learning settings.

projects.title: How Wikipedia frames controversial topics over time
projects.summary: Study how Wikipedia frames controversial topics and how this framing changes over time.

projects.title: Predicting Swiss popular vote outcomes from web information
projects.summary: Investigate whether the outcome of Swiss popular votes can be predicted from information available on the web before the vote.

projects.title: Alternatives to cross-validation for time series
projects.summary: Explore possible replacements for standard random-split cross-validation in time-series applications, where it is problematic.

projects.title: Heuristics for a toy model of COVID-19 contact tracing
projects.summary: Develop heuristics for a toy model that captures many challenges of COVID-19 contact tracing.

projects.title: Output sensitivity in the NAS-Bench-201 search space
projects.summary: Study output sensitivity in the NAS-Bench-201 search space, after a literature review of neural architecture search (NAS) algorithms, and compare the sensitivity metric with state-of-the-art NAS benchmarks in cost and performance.

projects.title: Quantifying the influence of lobbying on political decisions
projects.summary: Use quantitative methods from computer science and machine learning to assess to what extent lobbying is a hidden driver of political decisions.

projects.title: Visualizing the evolution of European laws
projects.summary: Data-mining project to visualize how European laws evolve over time, applying version-control ideas to legislation.

projects.title: Dataset and models of country interactions in UN climate negotiations
projects.summary: Collect and analyze a new dataset of collaborations and conflicts between countries in UN climate negotiations (COP), and develop models of these competitive dynamics.

projects.title: Meta-learning algorithms for semi-supervised few-shot classification
projects.summary: Investigate, implement and compare state-of-the-art meta-learning algorithms in a semi-supervised learning setting for few-shot classification.

projects.title: Unifying framework for meta-learning in classification and regression
projects.summary: Construct a unifying framework to compare meta-learning algorithms for classification and regression, and investigate algorithmic and theoretical improvements.

projects.title: Adding source localization algorithms to the INDY benchmark software
projects.summary: Implement existing source localization algorithms and add them to the benchmark software recently developed in the INDY lab.

projects.title: Reinforcement learning for active comparison-based search
projects.summary: Apply reinforcement learning to active search based on comparisons between items.

projects.title: Modeling people's perception of the magnitude of their actions
projects.summary: Develop an application to collect data on how people perceive the impact of their actions (e.g., flying vs. long showers) and implement a statistical model of that perception.

projects.title: Comparing and extending MeProp against Dropout
projects.summary: Compare the MeProp method with other regularization techniques such as Dropout, and explore extensions such as non-constant k over epochs, top-k vs random-k selection, or application to CNNs.

projects.title: Metric dimension of graphs under random perturbations
projects.summary: Analyse how the metric dimension of a graph changes under random perturbations. Aimed at students with a strong theoretical background.

projects.title: Search framework for the EPFL people database using profile photos
projects.summary: Develop a new search framework for navigating the database of EPFL people by comparing their profile photos.

projects.title: Scraping and modelling political texts
projects.summary: Scrape, mine, and model political texts to gain new insights from an existing large dataset, extending it with new data when needed. Open project where all ideas are encouraged.

projects.title: Detecting epidemic sources under misinformation about node states
projects.summary: Study how to handle misinformation about node states when detecting the source of an epidemic.

projects.title: Predicting end-to-end throughput in hybrid WiFi and power-line networks
projects.summary: In a hybrid WiFi and Power Line Communication network, find the optimal end-to-end route between access points given pairwise link capacities, mainly by predicting end-to-end throughput as a regression problem. No networking background required.

projects.title: Development and characterization of an acoustic matched source
projects.summary: The project aims to develop and characterize an acoustic matched source, using active control of a closed-box electrodynamic loudspeaker to achieve impedance matching. It includes a literature review, numerical FDTD/Simulink modelling, experimental measurements at multiple harmonics, and an extension to a broadband matched source using a corona discharge actuator.

projects.title: Enhancing Protein Design Through Advanced Graph Neural Networks
projects.summary: The project focuses on protein sequence design, creating protein sequences that perform specific functions for applications such as drug development and bioengineering. It will use advanced Graph Neural Networks to improve protein sequence design methods.

projects.title: Modeling translation elongation dynamics through Variational AutoEncoders
projects.summary: The project models ribosome profiling density profiles with Variational AutoEncoders to capture translation elongation dynamics. The student first evaluates VAE reconstruction in a single condition, then extends the decoder to take nutrient availability into account.

projects.title: Optimization of corona discharge loudspeakers
projects.summary: The project aims to identify and implement corona discharge loudspeaker configurations with better sound radiation efficiency, notably a useful band-pass behaviour over a wide audible band. It will build a COMSOL and/or analytical model of the transducer for geometry optimization, then build and test prototypes in anechoic conditions.

projects.title: Design of unprecedented sound sources: a dream come true with plasma loudspeakers?
projects.summary: The project aims to identify and, if possible, implement a purely omnidirectional corona discharge (plasma) loudspeaker configuration approximating an ideal pulsating sphere, and optionally extend the work to other canonical electroacoustic sources. The work involves COMSOL and/or analytical modelling for geometry optimisation, followed by prototype construction and anechoic testing.

projects.title: 3D Sound Localization
projects.summary: Build a toolbox that simulates human auditory localization to objectively assess how hearing aid algorithms preserve or distort spatial cues, replacing costly listening tests. The project has three stages: building a hearing-loss-aware 3D localization toolbox, measuring the HRTF of a Kemar dummy head, and validating the toolbox with listening tests involving about 10 normal-hearing and 20 hearing-impaired participants.

projects.title: Auditory distance perception
projects.summary: Evaluate how hearing aids affect the auditory distance perception of hearing-impaired listeners. The project has two stages: building a listening test facility with a loudspeaker on a precise motorised rail, then running listening tests with about 10 normal-hearing and 20 hearing-impaired participants.

projects.title: Exploration and improvement of a data-agnostic multimodal deep learning architecture relying on a novel fusion strategy
projects.summary: Explore, improve and propose alterations of a data-agnostic, perceiver-based multimodal deep learning architecture that integrates modalities sequentially. The work includes adapting layers for efficiency or performance, researching pre-training approaches, and evaluating data encoding tactics and hybrid fusion methods.

projects.title: Development of a Graphical User Interface for Electroacoustic Absorbers
projects.summary: The student reviews the literature on Electroacoustic Absorbers (EA), builds an analytical Matlab model, and implements direct impedance control on a prototype using a Speedgoat real-time target with Matlab/Simulink. The project ends with a stand-alone GUI that lets a non-expert set control parameters and assess an EA's acoustic performance in an impedance tube.

projects.title: Plasmacoustic headphones
projects.summary: Simulate and implement a fully open corona-discharge (CD) headphone, optimizing the transducer geometry with a COMSOL and/or analytical model, then building prototypes and testing them on an artificial ear in anechoic conditions. The goal is to avoid the occlusion effect of conventional headphones while managing sound leakage to the environment.

projects.title: Controlling the timbre of wind instruments with active control
projects.summary: Develop a scaled prototype of an active wind instrument: a cylindrical hollow duct with a ring of active electroacoustic absorbers that change the acoustic impedance and alter the timbre. The work covers COMSOL FEM simulations, design and control of the prototype, and acoustic assessment of the resonators and the whole instrument.

projects.title: VENOVA : an actively modified cylindrical cross-saxophone
projects.summary: The project aims to design an actuator and couplings (CAD and 3D printing) added to the VENOVA instrument, then model how impedance control at the actuator can alter its sound, and implement, measure and playtest control strategies. Some experience with reed instruments is preferable but not required.

projects.title: Controlling the timbre of wind instruments with active control
projects.summary: Studies wind instruments as axisymmetric hollow ducts with varying or constant cross-section, with the aim of controlling their timbre actively. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: Plasmacoustic headphones
projects.summary: Explores headphones based on the corona discharge principle, which can produce a linear acoustic flow velocity source without a conventional membrane. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: Development of a Graphical User Interface for Electroacoustic Absorbers
projects.summary: Aims to develop a graphical user interface for Electroacoustic Absorbers, which rely on a closed-box loudspeaker whose membrane is given a prescribed acoustic impedance. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: Exploration and improvement of a data-agnostic multimodal deep learning architecture relying on a novel fusion strategy
projects.summary: Explores and improves a data-agnostic multimodal deep learning architecture based on a novel fusion strategy for learning from multiple information channels (modalities).

projects.title: Auditory distance perception
projects.summary: Studies auditory distance perception, which supports spatial awareness, object localization and obstacle avoidance. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: 3D Sound Localization
projects.summary: Studies how sounds are localized in space, i.e. spatial hearing. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: Design of unprecedented sound sources: a dream come true with plasma loudspeakers?
projects.summary: Investigates spherical sound sources, considered an optimal geometry due to limited scattering, using plasma loudspeakers. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: Optimization of corona discharge loudspeakers
projects.summary: Aims to optimize corona discharge loudspeakers, which produce a linear acoustic flow velocity source without a conventional membrane. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: Modeling translation elongation dynamics through Variational AutoEncoders
projects.summary: Models translation elongation dynamics from ribosome profiling data, which measures codon-specific ribosome dwell times, using Variational AutoEncoders.

projects.title: Enhancing Protein Design Through Advanced Graph Neural Networks
projects.summary: Applies advanced graph neural networks to protein design, building on machine learning applications in biology.

projects.title: Development and characterization of an acoustic matched source
projects.summary: Develops and characterizes an acoustic matched source, drawing on nonlinear and time-varying systems in wave engineering. The page excerpt is truncated.

projects.title: VENOVA : an actively modified cylindrical cross-saxophone
projects.summary: Concerns an actively modified cylindrical cross-saxophone, a project described on the page as building on work by a team of engineers from Yamaha. The page excerpt is truncated.
